scope: A curated selection of short original excerpts and editorial reflections; not complete works.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: Begin the day prepared to meet interference, ingratitude, arrogance and selfishness. Their conduct comes from confusion about good and evil; your task is to remember the kinship of human beings and refuse to become like what obstructs you.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: At every hour, give your whole attention to the work at hand—with exactness, dignity and justice—and clear away every other thought. Treat each act as though it were your last.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: People seek retreats in the country, by the sea and in the hills. Yet nowhere is more peaceful than a well-ordered mind. Withdraw there briefly, restore yourself, and return to your duties.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: Do not live as if you had endless years ahead. Death is near; while life and power remain, use them well.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: When you resist getting up, remember what you were made for: the work of a human being. Plants, birds and ants perform their tasks; will you refuse yours for the sake of comfort?

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: What blocks a particular action need not block your purpose. The mind can adapt, turning impediment into material for character and useful action.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong-doer.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: Look within: let no action escape justice, and no thought escape understanding.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: If an external thing troubles you, the pain lies not in the thing but in your judgment of it—and you can revise that judgment now.

entries.author: Marcus Aurelius
entries.text: Your present task is simple: sound judgment now, action for the common good now, and a willing acceptance now of whatever arrives from outside.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Take possession of your time. Some hours are taken from us, others stolen, and others simply leak away. The most shameful loss is the one caused by carelessness.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Constantly changing books scatters the mind. Stay with a limited number of master thinkers long enough to digest what you read.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Philosophy asks for plain living, not theatrical austerity. Let your life be better than the crowd's, not ostentatiously unlike it.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Choose carefully whom you join. Association changes us: one person plants desire, another fear, another courage. Enter a crowd knowing that character is contagious.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: We are often more frightened than hurt, and suffer more from imagination than from reality. Test the fear against the facts before paying its full price.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Set aside a few days for plain food and rough clothing, then ask whether this is what you feared. Voluntary simplicity rehearses freedom from fortune.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: A change of scenery cannot cure what you carry within. You must change the mind, not merely the sky above it.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Remember that the person called a slave sprang from the same origin, breathes the same air, and is subject to the same fortune. Rank is an accident; humanity is shared.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: Life is not short by nature; we make it short by wasting it. We guard property closely while allowing others to trespass freely on our time.

entries.author: Seneca
entries.text: The best remedy for anger is delay. Its first heat asks for a verdict before the evidence has arrived; give reason time to recover the bench.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Some things depend on us: judgment, impulse, desire and aversion. Body, property, reputation and office do not. Freedom begins by keeping that boundary clear.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Men are disturbed, not by things, but by the principles and notions which they form concerning things.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Do not demand that events happen as you wish. Wish them to happen as they do, and your life will meet less useless friction.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: If you want to improve, be willing to appear foolish about external things. Progress cannot remain hostage to every spectator's opinion.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: When insulted, remember that your own opinion supplies the injury. Pause at the first impression; time makes self-command easier.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Before undertaking anything, consider what comes before and after it. Wanting the prize without accepting the training is a contract with disappointment.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: The faculty of choice can examine and govern itself; external faculties cannot. Put your seriousness where your authority actually lies.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: No one willingly assents to what appears false. When another acts badly, begin by asking what mistaken appearance persuaded him.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Materials are indifferent; the use you make of them is not. The ball is neither good nor bad—the art is in how it is played.

entries.author: Epictetus
entries.text: Train first in small things. Resist a minor impulse, endure a modest inconvenience, and build the faculty before asking it to carry a crisis.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: Consciousness does not emerge painlessly. Becoming aware often means surrendering a comfortable identification and tolerating the conflict that follows.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.work: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious
entries.text: Growth requires more than imagining oneself in the light. The neglected and disowned parts of the personality must also be brought into awareness.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: Self-knowledge develops through correction as well as discovery. Error is not outside the process; examined honestly, it becomes part of the education.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: Meaning can give modest circumstances more psychological weight than impressive achievements that feel empty.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: Lasting change begins with an honest acceptance of what is present. Condemnation alone drives the unwanted material further from conscious examination.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: A real encounter changes both people. Psychotherapy is not a one-way procedure performed on an object, but a relationship in which two personalities affect one another.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.text: Children learn chiefly from the character adults embody, not from the instructions adults recite. Example reaches where advice cannot.

entries.author: Carl Jung
entries.work: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
entries.text: The pendulum of the mind oscillates between sense and nonsense, not between right and wrong.
